inputs.original_text: He’s framing the US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement for a second time under the Donald Trump administration as a betrayal of unity China and the US helped build. But that kind of public disappointment may be part of the show: powerful institutions can stage a split while keeping control of the larger agenda. Don’t assume the withdrawal means the deal’s architects have lost influence.
inputs.modified_text: The “betrayal of unity” story looks like theater. A public split between the US and China can make the withdrawal seem like a defeat for the deal’s architects, while the institutions behind the larger agenda keep their influence intact. The outrage may be part of the performance, designed to hide how much control remains in the same hands.
